text: A neighbour asks whether the new park and ride scheme has made your commute easier. Give your honest opinion, including what works and what doesn't.

title: Commute small talk
text: Your friend asks why you were late again and you blame the school run traffic. Explain the morning chaos in a lively way.

title: Commute small talk
text: A colleague asks why you always seem so relaxed when you arrive at work. Explain your bus commute and how you use the time.

title: Commute small talk
text: You've started working from home two days a week and a friend asks if you miss commuting. Compare the two and say which you prefer.

title: Commute small talk

title: Pub

title: Pub

text: The landlord rings the bell and shouts "Last orders!" while you're mid-conversation. Persuade your friends to have one more before going home.

title: Pub
text: Your pub quiz team lost by one point because of a question about rivers. Tell a friend about the night, the argument over the answer, and your plans for revenge.

title: Pub
text: You've just had a disappointing Sunday carvery at a gastropub, where the roast potatoes were cold. Tell your partner what happened and whether you'll go back.

title: Pub

title: Pub

title: Pub
text: Your friend asks why the pub you go to is called a "free house". Explain what it means and why you prefer it.

text: Your five-a-side team has lost every match this season. Give a short pep talk in the changing room before tonight's game.

text: A visitor asks you to explain the Boat Race and why people watch it from the riverbank. Describe the event and recommend where to stand.

title: Sports chat
text: Your mate wants to become the manager of your Sunday league team. Tell him honestly whether he'd be good at it.

title: Sports chat
text: A neighbour sees you carrying your bowls bag and asks how you got into the sport. Tell them about the club and its members.

title: Sports chat
text: A friend asks you to recommend a sport for a complete beginner who wants to get fit and make friends. Suggest one and explain why.

title: Village fêtes and clubs
text: You're running the tombola at the village fête and the queue is building. Explain to the next customer how it works and persuade them to buy tickets.

title: Village fêtes and clubs
text: The village fête committee needs a new chair, and everyone is looking at you. Explain why you're willing to take it on and what you'd change.

title: Village fêtes and clubs
text: You've entered your Victoria sponge into the cake competition at the village fête. Describe it to the judge with some modest humour.

title: Village fêtes and clubs
text: The village hall needs a new roof and you're organising a fundraiser. Pitch your idea for a quiz and raffle to the parish committee.

title: Village fêtes and clubs
text: Tell a friend about the village fête where the dog show descended into chaos when a terrier stole the sausages from the barbecue.

title: Village fêtes and clubs
text: A neighbour asks whether you'd like to join the local am-dram society. Explain why you might, or why it's really not for you.

title: Village fêtes and clubs
text: You're a new member of the allotment society and the committee want to know about your plans for your plot. Describe what you hope to grow.

title: Village fêtes and clubs
text: Your friend has been roped into running the coconut shy at the school fair. Give them some advice on how to make it fun and profitable.

title: Village fêtes and clubs
text: The book club you've joined has picked a novel you found deeply boring. Give your honest view at the meeting without offending the person who chose it.

title: Village fêtes and clubs
text: You've joined a local walking group and a member asks how you're finding it. Tell them about your favourite walk so far.

title: Village fêtes and clubs
text: Your local brass band is struggling to recruit younger members. Make a short appeal at the village hall to persuade people to join.

title: Village fêtes and clubs
text: The village green is under threat from a housing development. Explain to a new resident why it matters to the community and what's being done.

title: Village fêtes and clubs
text: You're selling items at a jumble sale and a customer is haggling hard over a lamp. Negotiate a fair price with humour.

title: Village fêtes and clubs
text: You've been asked to host the quiz night at the cricket club for the first time. Introduce yourself and explain the rules to the teams.

title: Village fêtes and clubs
text: You've been asked to judge the scarecrow competition at the village fête and it's a tie. Explain your decision to the crowd diplomatically.

title: Village fêtes and clubs
text: The harvest festival is coming up and the school has asked for donations. Explain to your neighbour what's needed and how she can help.

title: Village fêtes and clubs
text: Your friend is thinking of joining the local morris dancing side and is worried about looking silly. Encourage them to give it a go.

title: Village fêtes and clubs
text: The garden club committee has asked you to give a short talk about your prize-winning roses. Describe how you grow them and offer tips.

title: Village fêtes and clubs
text: You've won the raffle at the village fête but the prize is something you really don't want. Respond graciously when the organiser hands it over.

title: School gate
text: Another parent at the school gate asks whether your child is enjoying Year 7. Give a friendly, honest update.

title: School gate
text: The parents' association is asking for volunteers for the summer fair and another parent asks if you'll help. Explain what you can and can't commit to.

title: School gate
text: A new parent at the school gate seems lost and doesn't know anyone. Introduce yourself and explain how things work at the school.

title: School gate
text: Another parent mentions that half-term starts next week and asks about your plans. Chat about what you're doing with the children.

title: School gate
text: Your child came home upset about something another child said. Raise it calmly with that child's parent at the school gate.

title: School gate
text: Parents' evening is tomorrow and another parent asks for advice, as it's their first one. Tell them what to expect and what questions to ask.

title: School gate
text: A parent asks if you'd be able to pick up her son after school on Thursday. Agree, and check the arrangements.

title: School gate
text: An INSET day has caught you by surprise and you need childcare. Ask a friend at the school gate whether her children could have yours for the day.

title: School gate
text: Tell a friend about the parents' group chat that has descended into a heated row about lost jumpers.

title: School gate
text: Another parent asks how you're finding the new head teacher, who has changed the uniform rules. Share a balanced opinion without getting drawn into gossip.

title: School gate
text: You're on the school run and another parent's car is blocking your drive again. Mention it to her lightly but clearly.

title: School gate
text: A parent at the gate asks whether you're worried about the catchment area for secondary schools. Talk through your thoughts on the choice ahead.

title: School gate
text: Your child has forgotten their PE kit for the third time this month. Ask another parent at the gate if there's a spare one anywhere.

title: School gate
text: The school is planning a sponsored walk and another parent wants your opinion on whether it's a good idea. Give your view and suggest how to get more families involved.

title: School gate
text: A parent you see every day finally introduces herself after two years. Respond warmly and make a bit of friendly conversation.

title: School gate
text: Another parent tells you their child is anxious about sitting the eleven-plus. Offer some reassurance and share what helped your family.

title: School gate
text: The lollipop lady outside the school is retiring after twenty years. Say a few words of thanks as parents gather to give her a card.

title: School gate
text: Another parent complains that the homework is far too much for their seven-year-old. Respond diplomatically, agreeing only up to a point.

title: School gate
text: You've been asked to help with the school nativity costumes and you can't sew. Explain your limitations to the organiser and offer something else instead.

title: School gate
text: A parent asks whether your child has settled in at nursery. Describe the first few weeks, tears and all.

title: School gate
text: Tell a friend about the school sports day where you were talked into the parents' race and fell over at the finish line.

title: School gate
text: Another parent asks your advice about whether to let their child walk to school alone for the first time. Share your thoughts and how you handled it.

title: School gate
text: The school has announced an unexpected closure because of a broken boiler. Discuss with another parent how you'll each manage childcare.

title: School gate
text: You're running late for pick-up and need another parent to collect your child. Ring her and explain, keeping it brief but grateful.

title: School gate
text: A new family has joined the class from abroad and the parents are unsure how British school terms work. Explain the term dates, half-terms and INSET days.

title: School gate
text: A parent asks if your child is coming to her son's fancy-dress birthday party on Saturday. Reply warmly, and check what your child should wear and bring.

title: Catching up
text: You've bumped into an old school friend you haven't seen for fifteen years. Catch up on what you've both been doing since you left.

title: Catching up
text: An old university friend has rung out of the blue. Tell them what's been happening in your life since graduation.

title: Catching up
text: A friend you lost touch with during a busy few years messages to suggest meeting up. Reply with a voice note explaining why you went quiet and suggesting a plan.

title: Catching up
text: You meet an old flatmate in a café and she asks how your love life is. Give a humorous update.

title: Catching up
text: An old friend tells you she's just quit her job to travel for a year. React and ask about her plans.

title: Catching up
text: You're having a long-overdue catch-up with your best friend, who has just had a baby. Ask about life with a newborn and share your own news.

title: Catching up
text: An old friend asks whether you're still in touch with the rest of your university group. Fill them in on what everyone's up to.

title: Catching up
text: You're meeting a childhood friend who has moved back to your home town after twenty years abroad. Tell them how the town has changed and where they should go.

title: Catching up
text: An old colleague you haven't seen in years has just been made redundant. Catch up and offer some encouragement without sounding patronising.

title: Catching up
text: You run into your old maths teacher in the supermarket. Tell them what you're doing now and thank them for something they did.

title: Catching up
text: Your old friend reminds you of a ridiculous holiday you went on together years ago. Retell the story from your side.

title: Catching up
text: You've just reconnected with a cousin after a long family fallout. Talk about how you both feel and suggest a fresh start.

title: Catching up
text: An old school friend asks whether you've still got that terrible haircut from Year 11. Respond with a laugh and an update.

title: Catching up
text: You're at a school reunion and someone you don't recognise is chatting to you as if you're best friends. Handle the situation gracefully.

title: Catching up
text: A friend has just moved to Manchester and you haven't seen her since. Ring her to find out how she's settling in and when you can visit.

title: Catching up
text: You haven't seen your godson since he was a toddler, and he's now off to university. Chat with him about his plans and offer some advice.

title: Catching up
text: An old friend says you look exactly the same as you did twenty years ago. Respond with some modest humour.

title: Catching up
text: You've caught up with your oldest friend over a long lunch and she's going through a hard time. Offer support and make plans to see her again soon.

title: Catching up
text: A friend from your gap year has come to stay. Reminisce about a memorable moment from your travels and how it changed you.

title: Funny story
text: Your family day out at the seaside featured a seagull stealing your chips, a parking ticket and an afternoon of rain. Tell a friend the whole saga with good humour.

title: Funny story
text: On a camping trip in Wales, your tent blew away in the night and you ended up sleeping in the car with your in-laws. Describe the weekend to a friend.

title: Funny story
text: You took your parents round a stately home and your dad set off the alarm by leaning on a priceless chair. Tell a colleague what happened next.

title: Funny story
text: Your narrowboat holiday ended with the boat stuck in a lock and a rescue by a group of cheerful pensioners. Tell your friends the story.

title: Funny story
text: On a theme park trip with your nephews, you were the only one who was sick on the rollercoaster. Describe the day to your sister.

title: Funny story
text: On a hen do in Blackpool, the coach broke down and you spent four hours at the motorway services in fancy dress. Tell a friend all about it.

title: Funny story
text: Your romantic picnic in the park was ruined by wasps, a rainstorm and a forgotten corkscrew. Describe it to a friend, making fun of yourself.

title: Funny story
text: On a walking holiday, you followed the Ordnance Survey map confidently for six miles in completely the wrong direction. Tell your colleagues how you realised.

title: Funny story
text: At a music festival, your wellies got stuck in the mud and you lost your phone, your friends and finally your tent. Describe the weekend to your flatmate.

title: Funny story
text: You bought tickets for a day at a county cricket match and spent the entire day sheltering from rain in the pavilion. Tell a friend how you passed the time.

title: Funny story
text: You took three toddlers to the zoo and everything went wrong, from a lost shoe to a meltdown at the penguins. Describe the day to another parent.

title: Funny story
text: At your cousin's wedding, you sat at the wrong table, spilt red wine on the bride's mother and were asked to make a speech without warning. Tell your flatmate everything.

title: Funny story
text: You booked a city break to York and discovered at reception that the hotel booking was for the following month. Explain to a friend how you rescued the weekend.

title: Funny story
text: You went punting in Cambridge and fell into the river in front of a crowd of tourists. Tell a friend how it happened and what you did next.

title: Funny story
text: During a driving lesson you stalled at a roundabout eight times while a busload of schoolchildren watched and cheered. Retell the moment to your colleagues.

title: Funny story
text: At a seaside B&B, the landlady locked the front door at ten sharp and you had to climb in through a window. Describe the night to a friend.

title: Funny story
text: Your day trip to the Highlands was so wet that the only thing you saw was the inside of a tea room. Tell a friend about it with dry humour.

title: Funny story
text: Your uncle set the garden fence on fire at the family barbecue and the fire brigade arrived during pudding. Describe the afternoon to a friend.

title: Funny story
text: You entered a cheese-rolling event and were knocked flat before the cheese had even left the top of the hill. Tell your mates how it went.

title: Funny story
text: You spent a whole week of a ski trip in the beginners' class with a group of five-year-olds. Describe the week to your friends.

title: Funny story
text: You turned up to a party dressed as a pirate, only to discover it wasn't fancy dress. Tell a colleague how you handled the evening.

title: Funny story
text: Your pub quiz team had the right answer to the jackpot question but wrote it down wrong. Describe the moment the answer was read out.

title: Funny story
text: On a coach tour of the Cotswolds, the driver got lost and you ended up reversing out of a farmyard. Tell your friends about the day.

title: Funny story
text: While volunteering at the village fête, you accidentally sold the vicar's bicycle at the jumble sale. Describe how you discovered the mistake and put it right.

title: Funny story
text: After a night out, you got on the wrong train, fell asleep and woke up at the end of the line. Tell your flatmate how you got home.

title: Funny story
text: You went wild swimming in a Scottish loch with friends and the water was so cold nobody lasted ten seconds. Describe the experience.

title: Funny story
text: The holiday cottage you rented in Cornwall had no phone signal, no hot water and an owner who swore it was haunted. Describe the week to a friend.

title: Funny story
text: You tried to impress a date by cooking a curry from scratch and set off every smoke alarm in the block. Describe the evening honestly.

title: Funny story
text: Your dad tried to use the self-service till at the supermarket and somehow summoned the manager three times. Describe the scene to your brother.

title: Funny story
text: You took your gran to the races for her birthday and she ended up winning more than the rest of the family put together. Tell a friend about the day.

title: Giving directions
text: A tourist outside the station asks you how to get to the cathedral. Give clear directions using local landmarks.

title: Giving directions
text: Someone stops you on the street to ask where the nearest cashpoint is. Give them simple directions.

title: Giving directions
text: A delivery driver rings because his sat nav can't find your house. Talk him through the last part of the route.

title: Giving directions
text: A visitor asks how to get from your town to the motorway while avoiding the rush-hour traffic. Give them the best route and a tip about where to stop.

title: Giving directions
text: A lost student on campus asks where the library is. Explain the route and what landmarks to look out for.
